interactions.summary: Jiang invites the room to answer why logic would be unnecessary in heaven, lets students propose thought-based communication and a Bruce Lee-style don't-think-feel analogy, then answers by sharply distinguishing institutional school logic from the imaginative freedom required to understand God and the Divine Comedy.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Jiang-led classroom exchange with multiple student replies

interactions.summary: A participant reads the next Paradise lines in which Beatrice's brief explanation removes one doubt but leaves Dante in a new perplexity.

claims.claim: Jiang says logic matters in high school because it is tied to tests, grades, and institutional evaluation rather than to the whole of reality.
claims.temporal_scope: Pedagogical and institutional claim made on 2026-06-15.

claims.claim: Jiang argues that logic is a system developed to control how people behave and think within our world.
Jiang says our world is only a subset of the entire universe, so the authority of logic is local rather than universal.
Jiang argues that mathematics and science can constrain a person's capacity to perceive the world.
Jiang says Dante will present logic as chains that keep the mind in a fixed mindset, while imagination behaves like a bird moving freely everywhere.
Jiang argues that to understand God and the Divine Comedy the mind must become birdlike, flying freely and following intuition.

signature_moments.moment: Logic is reduced to an institutional technology for passing tests and earning grades.
signature_moments.source_phrase: that's the point of logic, to take tests and to pass tests
signature_moments.why_it_matters: Jiang turns a supposedly universal faculty into a narrow disciplinary tool, which sharply lowers its spiritual authority.

signature_moments.moment: Logic becomes chains while imagination becomes a bird.
signature_moments.source_phrase: logic are like chains ... imagination is like a bird
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is the packet's cleanest reusable contrast for Jiang's broader argument that spiritual reading needs more than analytical constraint.

signature_moments.moment: Understanding God requires a mind willing to fly rather than stay locked in one mindset.
signature_moments.source_phrase: your mind has become almost like a bird and just fly around
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It converts imagination from optional style into the required posture for reading Dante's heaven.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Presented by Jiang as an institutional control system useful inside the human subset of reality but inadequate for heavenly understanding.
The freer faculty Jiang contrasts with logic and treats as necessary for understanding God and the Divine Comedy.
The inner guide Jiang says readers should follow once they stop treating logic as the sole route to understanding.

chronology_notes.note: Jiang marks several claims here as things that will become clearer later in the Divine Comedy, so the packet includes a forward-looking reading cue rather than a new dated position across sources.
